Note also that if $S$ denotes the involution acting on functions of $(x_{1},...,x_{N})$ by sending $x_{i}\mapsto x_{i}^{-1}$
for all $i$ , then we have $S\Gamma_{I}S=\Gamma_{I}^{-1}$ and
${\mathcal{D}}_{{\alpha};-n}^{q^{-1},t^{-1}}=S{\mathcal{D}}_{{\alpha};n}^{q,t}S$ , so that

$S\,{\mathfrak{e}}_{\alpha}(z)\,S=(-1)^{\alpha}\,{\mathfrak{f}}_{\alpha}(z^{-1})\ .$

The currents (3.4) can be explicitly expressed as

$\displaystyle{\mathfrak{e}}_{\alpha}(z)$
$\displaystyle=$
$\displaystyle\frac{q^{\frac{{\alpha}}{2}}}{(1-q)^{\alpha}}\sum_{|I|={\alpha},\,I\subset[1,N]}\delta(q^{{\alpha}/2}zx_{I})\prod_{i\in I\atop j\not\in I}\frac{\theta x_{i}-\theta^{-1}x_{j}}{x_{i}-x_{j}}\,\Gamma_{I},$

$\displaystyle{\mathfrak{f}}_{\alpha}(z)$
$\displaystyle=$
$\displaystyle\frac{q^{-\frac{{\alpha}}{2}}}{(1-q^{-1})^{\alpha}}\sum_{|I|={\alpha},\,I\subset[1,N]}\delta(q^{-{\alpha}/2}zx_{I})\prod_{i\in I\atop j\not\in I}\frac{\theta^{-1}x_{i}-\theta x_{j}}{x_{i}-x_{j}}\,\Gamma_{I}^{-1},$

by use of the formal $\delta$ function (3.2).

Note that the finite number $N$ of variables implies the vanishing relations:

(3.6)

${\mathfrak{e}}_{N+1}(z)=0\ \ {\rm and}\ \ {\mathfrak{f}}_{N+1}(z)=0.$

3.1.4. Main result

We call ${\mathfrak{e}}(z):={\mathfrak{e}}_{1}(z)$ and ${\mathfrak{f}}(z):={\mathfrak{f}}_{1}(z)$ the fundamental currents. Our main result is that these satisfy relations in the quantum toroidal algebra, as suggested by the notation. We will see later that the vanishing condition (3.6) implies a certain quotient of the algebra by polynomials of degree $N+1$ in the fundamental generators.
card.label: Remark 3.3

paper.title: (t,q) Q-systems, DAHA and quantum toroidal algebras via generalized Macdonald operators
paper.abstract: We introduce difference operators on the space of symmetric functions which are a natural generalization of the $(q,t)$-Macdonald operators. In the $t\to\infty$ limit, they satisfy the $A_{N-1}$ quantum $Q$-system. We identify the elements in the spherical $A_{N-1}$ DAHA which are represented by these operators, as well as within the quantum toroidal algebra of $gl_1$ and the elliptic Hall algebra. We present a plethystic, or bosonic, formulation of the generating functions for the generalized Macdonald operators, which we relate to recent work of Bergeron et al. Finally we derive constant term identities for the current that allow to interpret them in terms of shuffle products. In particular we obtain in the $t\to\infty$ limit a shuffle presentation of the quantum $Q$-system relations.
